FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pulut durian

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the flesh of {0_adj} broken down in a hot {1_adj} milk sweetened with palm {2_plur}, scented with pandan. Eaten warm with a spoon, somewhere between a cream and a soup.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a paste of sticky {1_adj} flour, palm {2_adj} and the flesh of {0_adj}, stirred without stopping for six hours in a cauldron until it turns almost black and pulls away from the sides.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a skin of sticky {1_adj} dough filled with cold {0_adj} flesh. The dough holds the smell in until the first bite, which makes it a formidable practical joke.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a Vietnamese cake of spiralled puff pastry, filled with a paste of {0_adj} and a salted {2_adj} yolk at the centre. The layers peel apart one by one at the cut.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an uncooked snow-skin dough pressed in a seal, filled with the flesh of {0_adj} and a sweetened {2_adj} paste. Served iced, unlike the classic mooncake.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: twenty very fine pancakes stacked up, each parted from the next by a layer of {0_adj} flesh folded into whipped {2_plur}. Cut clean, and eaten iced.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: small choux buns filled with a pure {0_adj} cream, served cold. Sold in refrigerated boxes in Singapore, and banned on the underground like everything else containing that fruit.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an uncooked {1_adj} filling loaded with the flesh of {0_adj}, set in the cold a whole night. The cheese rounds off the fruit and makes it approachable to the uninitiated.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a very airy sponge into whose raw batter the flesh of {0_adj} is folded. The smell fills the kitchen while it bakes and settles there for the day.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: durian ice cream
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a {1_adj} and {2_adj} base in which the fruit goes in raw, with no cooking to soften its scent. The cold tames it a little; a little only.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tempoyak
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the flesh of {0_adj} salted and left to ferment a week in a closed jar, until it turns sour and creamy. It is no longer a fruit at that stage: it is a condiment, and it keeps for months.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sambal tempoyak
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: fermented {0_coll} pounded in the mortar with {1_plur} and {2_plur}, then briefly fried. The acidity of the fermentation stands in for the tamarind one would use elsewhere.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a yellow curry built on {1_adj} milk and turmeric, soured with fermented {0_plur} rather than with tamarind. The sauce takes on a thickness no other acid will give it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: ikan patin tempoyak
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: river {1_coll} stewed in fermented {0_coll} and {2_coll}, with no coconut milk at all. The emblematic dish of Pahang and Jambi, and the best demonstration that this fruit is not only a dessert.
